hook: Your productivity system is probably the thing keeping you unproductive.
topic: The planning paradox — sophisticated systems as advanced avoidance
body:
**Your productivity system is probably the thing keeping you unproductive.**

This is uncomfortable, but consider it. The more sophisticated your system — the more apps, the more colour-coded calendars, the more carefully structured time blocks — the more daily maintenance that system requires. And every minute spent managing the system is a minute not spent on the output the system was built to produce.

There's a specific type of high-functioning procrastinator who is genuinely excellent at building systems. They can show you their Notion workspace. They can explain their task hierarchy. They have a morning routine. What they cannot show you is consistent output on the work that matters, because the system has become a substitute for it.

Organisation is not output. A perfect calendar does not contain a single finished thing.

The reframe: the best productivity system is the one that requires the least management. Complexity is a signal that the system is serving the wrong function — it's serving the need to feel organised, not the need to produce.

One action: cut your productivity setup to two components — a list of today's two most important outputs, and a timer. Everything else is optional.

Full framework in the link in bio.
